text.p: Pharmaceutical giant Pfizer Inc. said Tuesday its earnings rose in the first quarter due to sales of products launched in the last few years, including drugs for treating Alzheimer's disease and high cholesterol.

Pfizer's earnings for the first quarter were $602 million, a 16 percent increase over the $517 million earned a year ago in the same period. Earnings per share were 93 cents, up 15 percent over the 81 cents earned in the same period last year.
"This quarter's performance shows the power of our current line of innovative new products, launched over the last few years," said Chairman William Steere Jr.

He noted that Aricept, a drug for treating Alzheimer's disease, and Lipitor, used for treating pateints with high cholesterol levels, which New York-based Pfizer is co-promoting with other drug companies, have been well received in the medical community.
But Steere noted that the strength of the dollar could hurt earnings for the full year.
"Given the strength of the dollar, foreign exhange, at current exchange rates, would reduce sales and income growth for the full year by two or three percentage points," he said.
Pfizer reported that first quarter sales rose 12 percent to $3 billion.

By segment, health care sales increased by 12 percent, pharmaceuticals sales increased by 17 percent in the United States and by 11 percent internationally, animal health sales grew by 10 percent, and consumer health segment sales were up 14 percent, the company said.
Steere said Pfizer plans to spend $2 billion on research and development in 1997 and will launch six new products in the next three years.
A spokesman said the company spent $1.68 billion on research and development for all of 1996. Pfizer stock fell 50 cents to $85.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
